entities.summary: Zerai Deres was an Eritrean revolutionary and translator. In 1938, he engaged in an act of public devotion to an important symbol of his native country, the Monument to the Lion of Judah, at the time kept in Rome. When interrupted, he violently protested against Italian colonialism while brandishing a scimitar, which led to his arrest and internment in a psychiatric hospital for seven years, until his death. However, contemporary Italian historians doubt the claim that he was mentally unstable. Zerai's protest, lionized after the end of the Second World War, is considered by Eritrean and Ethiopian historiography as part of the movement against Italian occupation.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Zerai Deres' protest against Italian colonialism in 1938 contributed to the movement against occupation, with his act of defiance inspiring Eritrean and Ethiopian historiography. His legacy serves as a symbol of resistance against colonial powers.
